samples.summary: `setCursorForHistory()`'s documented synchronous presence flush is silently dropped inside a batch, so any batched mutation path staged through it will record the wrong reverse presence
samples.evidence: `setCursorForHistory` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3039-3045) exists precisely to flush the pre-edit caret/selection into presence before a mutation — its own comment at :3032-3037 says "the pre-edit selection must already be in presence when the mutation runs. Without this flush, select-then-immediately-type could record a stale/collapsed selection as the reverse." It implements that by calling `this.updateCursorPos(...)`, and this change makes `updateCursorPos` return early (`if (this.skipNonHistoryPresence()) return;`) whenever a batch is open. So inside a batch the flush becomes a no-op while the mutation's `recordHistoryPresence(..., {addToHistory:true})` still runs, and Yorkie captures whatever stale presence happened to be there as the reverse — undo restores the wrong caret/selection. The five editor call sites that rely on this flush are packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1031, :1152, :1997, :2206, :3052. None of them is inside a batch today (only `withNamedStyleChange` opens one, and it does not call `setCursorForHistory`), which is why this is currently latent rather than broken — but the diff itself advertises the merge/split sweeps as the next callers of `batch()`, and those paths *do* go through `setCursorForHistory`. Nothing warns at the seam: `skipNonHistoryPresence()`'s comment says "skipping loses nothing: presence is last-write-wins and the next cursor move republishes", which is true for the throttled live-cursor publish but not for the history-staging use. Fix belongs on the new code — either exempt the `setCursorForHistory` flush from the skip, or document the restriction in the `DocStore.batch()` contract.

samples.summary: `MemDocStore.undo()`/`redo()` inside a batch silently corrupt the checkpoint the batch pushed, where `YorkieDocStore` is a safe no-op — the same store-divergence the change explicitly guarded against for `setDocument()`
samples.evidence: The new contract in packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:73 says "Do not call `undo()` / `redo()` from inside a batch", and the branch's own lessons file (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-store-batch-seam-lessons.md:42-43) records that under Yorkie this is *already* harmless because `history.canUndo()` is false while `isUpdating`. `MemDocStore.undo()` (memory.ts:157-161) has no such protection: called inside a batch it pops the checkpoint `batch()` just pushed and assigns it to `this.doc`, after which the `wroteNothing` comparison in batch()'s finally (memory.ts:230-232) sees `undoStack[last] !== before`, keeps no checkpoint, and leaves the store with a reverted document plus a polluted redo stack. That is exactly the asymmetry the change went out of its way to close for `setDocument()` (a Mem-side throw "for parity, so code written and tested against it would pass and then throw under the collaborative store") — here the polarity is reversed: code written against Yorkie is a harmless no-op and silently corrupts history under the in-package store used by the docs package, the visual harness (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/visual/docs-scenarios.tsx:108) and the hunt harness (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:503). I found no current caller that reaches `undo()` inside an open batch, so this is a latent gap rather than a live break.

samples.summary: Task/design record describes the presence-inside-batch behaviour that the branch does NOT ship, and the `DocStore.batch()` contract omits the presence rule entirely
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-store-batch-seam-todo.md:111-116 states that all 30 `doc.update` call sites "now go through `withUpdate`, including the two presence-only writes (`publishResolvedLocalCursor`, `updateCursorPos`) — a presence write that fired synchronously inside an open batch would otherwise nest an update. Presence `set` is not part of the document change, so folding it in does not pollute the batch's undo unit." The shipped code does the opposite: `skipNonHistoryPresence()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3193) makes both of those writes return *without* publishing inside a batch. The user-visible rule "non-history presence writes are dropped inside a batch" also appears nowhere in the shared contract (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:62-85) nor in docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:288-311, which is where every other batch rule (nesting, undo/redo, setDocument) is enumerated — so the one behaviour that differs between the two implementations is documented only in a private method comment. Not caught by any lane: the top-level design-doc link check does not verify prose, and nothing checks task files.
